title: Undirected graph connectivity

problem.name: Undirected graph connectivity
problem.statement_latex:
Given an undirected graph $G$, decide whether $\forall u,v\in V$ there is a path from $u$ to $v$; optionally return its connected components and a spanning forest. Connectivity is a feasibility condition in network design.
The quantum and classical bounds count adjacency-matrix or neighbor-array queries; explicit graph traversal time is also stated.
problem.statement_text: Given an undirected graph $G$, decide whether $\forall u,v\in V$ there is a path from $u$ to $v$; optionally return its connected components and a spanning forest. Connectivity is a feasibility condition in network design. The quantum and classical bounds count adjacency-matrix or neighbor-array queries; explicit graph traversal time is also stated.

quantum.headline_latex: $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ matrix queries or $\Theta(n)$ array queries, quantum graph exploration.
quantum.headline_text: $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ matrix queries or $\Theta(n)$ array queries, quantum graph exploration.
quantum.details_latex: The array model includes the vertex degrees and indexed coherent access to each neighbor list. The algorithm can also output connected components and a spanning forest with the same asymptotic query bound. The forest has $O(n)$ edges.
quantum.details_text: The array model includes the vertex degrees and indexed coherent access to each neighbor list. The algorithm can also output connected components and a spanning forest with the same asymptotic query bound. The forest has $O(n)$ edges.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n^2)$ matrix queries; $O(n+m)$ explicit-input time, breadth-first or depth-first search.
classical.headline_text: $\Theta(n^2)$ matrix queries; $O(n+m)$ explicit-input time, breadth-first or depth-first search.
classical.details_latex: The matrix lower bound follows from distinguishing two disconnected components from a graph with one hidden connecting edge. Array traversal visits every discovered vertex and its incident edges. The quantum linear-query result uses the symmetry of undirected neighbor access and the supplied degrees.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial: $n^2\to n^{3/2}$ in the matrix model and $n+m\to n$ in the array comparison. Quantum search accelerates structured graph exploration.
strength.description_text: Polynomial: $n^2\to n^{3/2}$ in the matrix model and $n+m\to n$ in the array comparison. Quantum search accelerates structured graph exploration.

evidence.description_latex: A rigorous query separation, with matching quantum upper and lower bounds.

hardware.description_latex: Fault-tolerant implementation uses $O(\log n)$ active vertex registers, coherent neighbor-oracle workspace and $O(n\log n)$ classical forest records. Constructing or accessing the graph oracle contributes to the gate count.
